Langstrasse — Zurich, Switzerland

⚪ Limited-data assessment · district burglary data shown alongside Methodology →

Higher caution advised day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Zurich's best-known nightlife and red-light district — lively and genuinely popular, but with well-documented incidents; local press has explicitly noted that tourists have been warned against booking hotels near Langstrasse. A two-faced neighborhood, much like Porta Palazzo in Turin — which is exactly the pattern that inspired this whole project.

This link is already scoped to this area (not the whole city), using the neighbourhood's real coordinates.

This is a limited-data assessment. Zurich publishes no neighbourhood-level crime dataset, and this area has not yet had a full source review, so the rating is indicative and is labelled as such rather than presented as evidenced.
Real official data point: Langstrasse sits in Kreis 4, one of Zurich's 12 police districts. Kantonspolizei Zürich recorded an average of 6.07 break-ins a year per 1,000 premises — homes and workplaces together — in that district across 3 years (2025, 2024, 2023), 186% of the 12-district average of 3.26 per 1,000 premises. Workplaces are counted because some districts hold far more of them than residents — Kreis 1 has 5,583 residents and 78,087 jobs — and dividing by residents alone made the old town read as the worst district in the city, which the counts behind it do not support. This figure is real, current, and official — but it covers burglaries only (not the full range of crime types) and is reported at the district level, not for Langstrasse specifically, so treat it as directional context for the wider area rather than a rating of this exact neighbourhood.

Frequently asked questions

Is Langstrasse safe?

Wandroz currently rates Langstrasse in Zurich as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Zurich, both by day and after dark. This is a limited-data assessment: Zurich publishes no neighbourhood-level crime dataset and this area has not yet had a full source review, so the rating is indicative and labelled as such rather than presented as evidenced.

Is Langstrasse safe at night?

At night, Langstrasse is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Zurich. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Langstrasse a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Langstrasse's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Zurich) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. The Booking.com link on this page searches Langstrasse itself.

Is there any official crime data for Langstrasse?

Partially. Langstrasse sits in Kreis 4, one of Zurich's 12 police districts. Kantonspolizei Zürich publishes a real, current burglary rate for that district — 6.07 break-ins a year per 1,000 premises (homes and workplaces), 186% of the 12-district average. This covers burglaries only, not all crime types, and is reported at district level, not specifically for Langstrasse — see the box below for the full figure and caveats. The neighbourhood-wide rating above is still the limited-data assessment described above, not derived from this burglary figure.
